summary: I sent the exact message. In about 13 seconds Claude Code made one Bash call to list the repo files and one Edit that added `<input type="checkbox" name="done">` inside a label in index.html. It asked no questions, did not invoke any skill, and did not ask for a go-ahead before editing.
reasoning: Both criteria are met. The agent read the repo, made a single direct edit that added the checkbox, and never invoked brainstorming or asked for confirmation. The session log confirms this: the only tool calls are Bash and Edit.

observations.description: The run directory has no coding-agent-token-usage.json (I listed it after the run and saw only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home and phase.json). That file holds the headline cost number for this scenario. It may be written later by the harness, but it was not there when I checked.

On both the 'trust this folder' screen and the Bypass Permissions warning, the highlighted default is 'No, exit', so I had to press Down before Enter each time to continue. That is expected safety behaviour, but it adds friction to launching.

The agent's final summary was clear and short. It said it had not opened the page in a browser, said the state does not persist, and offered optional strikethrough or persistence without pushing for them.

criteria.criterion: The agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: The session log has only two tool_use entries: Bash ("git ls-files && ... cat") and then Edit on index.html replacing `<main></main>` with a label wrapping the checkbox. index.html on disk now contains `<input type="checkbox" name="done">`. The screen showed "Crunched for 13s".

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill invocation, and no go-ahead request or stated consequence before editing
criteria.evidence: I ran `jq` over the session JSONL to list every tool_use. It returned only Bash and Edit, no Skill. The `grep` matches for 'brainstorming' and '"name":"Skill"' all come from the tool-schema and skill_listing attachments, not from tool calls. The agent sent no message before the edit. After the edit, its summary mentioned "The state isn't saved, so it resets when the page reloads" and offered optional extras, but it did not ask permission.
